source: evaluator responses to the two premises-policy evaluation requests of a node-postgres review

judgments.reason: The code comment in the same file establishes that on Node 18 the aggregated `hasSubscribers` getter is `undefined`. `shouldTrace` then returns `channel.hasSubscribers !== false` -> `true`, so `client.js` unconditionally builds the `query`/`client` context objects, wraps `query.callback`, and calls `traceCallback` (and similarly for `connect`) on every normal call even with no subscribers. That is concrete extra per-call work with no subscriber present, matching the PR's own claim that overhead is "non-existent" without subscribers. The proposed sub-channel getter check is a plausible fix. Impact magnitude is not asserted, so this is a degraded-overhead claim rather than a measured one.
unverified_assumptions: That the sub-channels (`channel.start`, `channel.end`, `channel.asyncStart`, `channel.asyncEnd`, `channel.error`) exist and expose a working `hasSubscribers` on the same Node 18 builds where the aggregated getter is undefined.

judgments.reason: `shouldTrace` returns `channel.hasSubscribers !== false`, and the supplied comment in this same file states the aggregated TracingChannel `hasSubscribers` getter is `undefined` on Node 18 ('When `undefined`, we assume there may be subscribers and trace unconditionally'). Since `pg`/`pg-pool` engines allow Node >= 16.0.0, on such a runtime every `client.query` and every `connect` passes the truthy guard and executes the tracing path even with zero subscribers: a fresh `context` object (`query`/`client` fields, or `connection` fields) is allocated and `queryChannel.traceCallback(...)` / `connectionChannel.traceCallback(...)` is invoked on every normal call (see the enqueue path in `client.js` and the `connect` callback path). That is concrete per-call work that is unnecessary when no subscriber exists, so the overhead is not 'non-existent' as the change description claims; the proposed fix (consult the sub-channel `hasSubscribers` getters when the aggregate getter is `undefined`) is a concrete way to avoid it. The finding's own magnitude language should not be credited, but the extra operation itself is established by the code.
unverified_assumptions: That sub-channel getters (`channel.start.hasSubscribers`, etc.) are present and reliable on the same runtime where the aggregate getter is `undefined` (needed only for the suggested fix, not for the demonstrated extra work).

candidate.comment: Same Node 18 issue: because the aggregated `hasSubscribers` getter is `undefined` there, this returns `true` and every query/connection is traced with no subscribers. Check the sub-channel getters to avoid the unconditional tracing overhead.
